_README: One entry per discussion question. The key is the item_id you set in
the Qualtrics JavaScript (ITEM_ID). Keys starting with _ are ignored.
question  - the stem, copied exactly as participants see it.
options   - the answer choices. Used for YOUR records and for leak
detection. These are NOT shown to the model.
correct   - the true answer. Never shown to the model.
targets   - participant's answer -> the answer the model steers to.
hints     - target answer -> the ABSTRACT claim the model argues.
This is what the model actually sees. It never sees the
option text, so it cannot quote it back. Write these at
the level of a principle, not a conclusion: if the hint
names which listed factors count, the model will too.
default_target - used when the participant's answer is not a key in
IMPORTANT: keys inside 'targets' must match the choice text Qualtrics
pipes over, character for character, or the server falls back to
default_target. Check prior_answer in sessions.csv after a pilot run.

item_01.question: You lift a suitcase from the floor to a table. In addition to the weight of the suitcase, select all of the following factors that determine the work done by the gravitational force on the suitcase. (1) whether you lift it directly up to the table or along a longer path (2) whether you lift it quickly or slowly (3) the height of the table above the floor
_targets_rationale: Participant WRONG  -> model argues for the correct answer.
Participant RIGHT  -> model argues for '(1) and (3) only', the
path-dependence misconception, which is the most plausible
distractor here. This arm measures induced errors.
Together these give you both quantities in one design. If you only
want one, change this map before collecting data, not after.

hints.(3) only: The force in question belongs to a class whose effect over a journey is fixed by the start and end points alone. Argue from that principle. Do not say which of the listed factors it rules in or out - make them work that out.
hints.(1) and (3) only: Work is force acting over a distance, so the journey itself is part of the physical picture and a longer journey means more of it. Argue from that principle. Do not say which of the listed factors it rules in or out.

_hints_note: The model sees ONLY the hint for the target it is steering to, never
the option text and never the word 'only'. Rewrite a hint if replies
are still too revealing - that is the main dial you have.
_giveaway_note: Phrases that, if the model writes them, mean it has handed over the
answer in words even though it quoted no option. A reply containing
one is thrown away and regenerated. Add to this list whenever you
read a pilot transcript that gives too much away.
